lead.kicker: TOP STORY  •  SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN
lead.headline: Houthi Missile Hits Saudi Oil Company Office
lead.deck: The war in Yemen has now reached Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil company.
body: Yemen is a country just south of Saudi Arabia. A group there called the Houthis is fighting its government, which Saudi Arabia backs. In recent days the Houthis have aimed missiles at Saudi targets.

On Saturday, a missile hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia’s capital. Saudi aviation officials say at least 13 people were killed and more than 300 were hurt. On Tuesday, a ballistic missile hit an office building at the Dhahran base of Aramco, the Saudi oil company. Saudi news said there was a small fire and nobody was hurt. The Houthis claimed it and promised more attacks on airports and oil sites.

Saudi Arabia answered by striking an oil site near Sanaa, Yemen’s capital. The Saudi-led coalition told civilians to leave an oil depot in the city. President Trump says the United States is thinking about joining Saudi Arabia’s side. Asked if it would, he said, “We may.”

map.title: THE RED SEA
map.footnote: A long, narrow sea between two continents
map.caption: Saudi Arabia and Yemen sit on the eastern shore of the Red Sea.

lead.why: Airports and oil sites serve people far from the fighting. When they are hit, travel and fuel prices can feel it, and a wider war becomes more likely.

world.headline: Oil Stays Above $100 as Ships Are Attacked
world.deck: The cost of fuel has jumped since the war with Iran began.
body: Oil is the thick liquid, pumped from underground, that is made into petrol and diesel. It is sold by the barrel. On Tuesday, a barrel of the kind called Brent closed at $105.69. Another kind, called WTI, closed at $94.14.

Much of the oil that fuels the world passes through the Strait of Hormuz. A strait is a narrow sea passage. This one lies between Iran and its neighbours. Senior Iranian officials told the news agency Reuters that Iran has used new tactics against ships there for about 10 days. They said the aim is to keep oil prices high. A group that tracks shipping reported that a container ship was hit by a projectile in the strait. An Iranian naval officer said Iran was waiting to sink approaching US warships. The US military’s Central Command rejected that and said US and partner forces control the strait.

Families feel it at the pump. The American Automobile Association says petrol in the United States now averages $4.33 a gallon. Before the war began it was $2.98. Diesel, the fuel for trucks, averages $6.29.

chart.title: PRICE AT THE PUMP
chart.subtitle: US average a gallon; first bar is petrol
chart.caption: Prices are from AAA, as reported on Wednesday.

world.connect: Geography matters here. A strait is like a doorway: if ships are scared to pass through the narrow doorway, oil can reach buyers more slowly, and sellers can charge more.

us.headline: Hurricane Isaias Leaves Six Dead in Florida
us.deck: More than 45,000 customers were still without power on Tuesday.
body: A hurricane is a huge, spinning storm with strong winds and heavy rain. Hurricane Isaias came ashore near Destin, on Florida’s Gulf Coast, on Friday night. It was a Category 2 storm, with gusts up to 118 miles an hour.
On Tuesday, Florida’s governor, Ron DeSantis, said six people had died in the state. Deaths included a falling tree during cleanup and a car crash. Two more people died in Alabama.

Then came the long clean-up. At the worst point, more than 400,000 Florida customers lost power. About 95 percent have it back, but over 45,000 were still waiting, mainly in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties. Early estimates put the cost to Escambia County alone at about $64 million.
us.why: A storm’s danger lasts after the wind stops. Power, clean-up and medical care decide how quickly a community recovers.

india.headline: Opposition Takes Voter-List Fight to the Supreme Court
india.deck: Rahul Gandhi and other leaders want the revision of India’s voter lists suspended.
body: A voter list is the official list of people allowed to vote. India’s Election Commission has been carrying out a Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, of these lists. Opposition parties say it is flawed. The Commission rejects allegations of wrongdoing. Opposition leaders have also called for the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to resign.

On Monday, Rahul Gandhi, the leader of the opposition, and other opposition leaders filed a petition in the Supreme Court. A petition is a formal request to a court. It asks the court to suspend the revision across all States for now. It also asks for a committee led by a retired Supreme Court judge to check the removals, and for no name to be taken off the list without notice and a hearing.

The court is due to hear the plea on Thursday, before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi. On 5 October, the court sent notices to the government and the Commission over the revision. It said that if the law was not followed, it can undo the decisions. On Sunday, the Chief Justice declined a request from Mr Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge to meet him. He said the issues were already before the court.
india.why: Voter lists decide who can vote. A court case shows how even an independent election body can be questioned.
